searchText: Fun fact: once in the past the plan was 320 ETH The problem with this is the more people participate the heavier the beacon chain gets. If we will lower the stake size to 3.2 ETH, the beacon chain will get 10x as heavy. In PoW, however, there is no such thing. I’m pro-PoW myself too, but unfortunately there is nothing we can do here. People who govern ETH decided that ETH will go PoS and that’s it. 402kg CO2 for 1 Bitcoin transaction, no big deal ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Yet another intelligent discussion with PoS shill Q: https://t.co/3g1GUvuA3A in reference to VB's reddit post on the future is multichain, im wondering what are the current thoughts are on bridges with long time delays, like 1 month, (also, where's the right room to post this question?) just buy more then There's no such assumption in those notes as the concentration of capital is irrelevant for the argument he's making. Overhead in messages per seconds is the bottleneck and the number is chosen so that the validating set is the maximum we can handle. If there was only one account holding 32Eth, still this number would be the best we could do now in PoS That paragraph precisely makes a point about maximizing the validating set while tolerating the overhead. There is absolutely nothing there about capital distribution
